'''Francisco Enrique La Marca Gutiérrez''' (born 11 August 1957)<ref name=":0">{{cite book |last1=Adler |first1=Kraig |title=Contributions to the History of Herpetology |url=https://archive.org/details/contributionstoh0000unse_j9m0 |date=8 August 2012 |publisher=Society for the Study of Amphibians and Reptiles |location=Vancouver, Canada |isbn=978-0-916984-82-3 |page=[https://archive.org/details/contributionstoh0000unse_j9m0/page/428 428] |edition=3 |access-date=30 December 2022}}</ref> is a Venezuelan [[herpetologist]] and tropical ecologist. 

==Biography==
He is the son of Vincenzo La Marca Zirini (b. 1926 in Noto, Sicily, Italy) and María Eduvina Gutiérrez.<ref>{{cite book |last=Guerra Ucello |first=Vincenzo |title=Los Brazos Abiertos de Venezuela |url=https://catalog.loc.gov/vwebv/search?searchCode=LCCN&searchArg=91818478&searchType=1&permalink=y |access-date=6 June 2023 |publisher=Editorial Badeven |location=Caracas |page=275 |date=July 1985}}</ref> He was a disciple of [[Hobart M. Smith]] ([[University of Colorado Boulder]]) and [[John D. Lynch]] ([[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]]).<ref>{{cite journal |title=Biological and systematic synopsis of a genus of frogs from Northern mountains of South America (Anura: Dendrobatidae: Mannophryne) |date=30 June 1995 |journal=Bulletin of the Maryland Herpetological Society |volume=31 |issue=2 |page=56}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Conant |first=Roger |title=A Field Guide to the Life and Times of Roger Conant |year=1997 |publisher=Selva; Cayonlands Publishing Group, L.C. |isbn=0-9657446-0-4 |location=Provo, Utah, USA |pages=363–364 |language=English |chapter=Chapter 59. The Last Continent: Part I. Venezuela}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite book |title=Aposematic Poison Frogs (Dendrobatidae) of the Andean Countries: Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Perú and Venezuela |year=2016 |publisher=Conservation International |isbn=978-1-934151-27-3 |editor1=Ted R. Kahn |editor2=Enrique La Marca |editor3=Stefan Lötters |editor4=Jason L. Brown |editor5=Evan Twomey |editor6=Adolfo Amézquita |location=Arlington, Virginia, USA |page=vi |language=English}}</ref>

He has worked in [[teaching]] (professor of Biogeography) and in [[research]] (Curator of the Collection of Amphibians and Reptiles, Laboratory of Biogeography, School of Geography), at the [[University of the Andes (Venezuela)|University of the Andes]], in [[Mérida, Mérida|Mérida]], [[Venezuela]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Vertebrados Actuales y Fósiles de Venezuela |year=1997 |publisher=Editorial Venezolana C.A. |isbn=980-221-877-4 |location=Mérida, Venezuela |page=iv}}</ref>

He is a retired full professor at the University of the Andes (ULA), dedicated for more than 40 years to the study of Venezuelan herpetofauna. He is the taxonomic author of species in the class Amphibia (order Anura) and in the class Reptilia (orders Sauria and Serpentes).<ref name=":0" /> He has described 42 new species of amphibians and reptiles.<ref name=lamarca/> 

His scientific output includes six books and more than 200 articles, most of them published in specialized journals. He has traveled to twenty-three countries with field explorations in fifteen of them, in South, Central, and North America, as well as Europe and Africa. He studied [[biology]] at ULA (Mérida, Venezuela) and at the [[University of Colorado]] (Boulder, CO, USA, under the supervision of Dr. Hobart Smith); earned a master's degree in Systematics and Biogeography at the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]] (Lincoln, NE, USA, under Dr. John D. Lynch); and later obtained a doctorate in Tropical Ecology at ULA (under Drs. Guillermo Sarmiento and John D. Lynch).<ref name=":1" /><ref name=lamarca/> 

He has been assistant curator at the Museum of Zoology of the University of Colorado, Boulder; president of the Biogeos Foundation for the Study of Biological Diversity; Chief Coordinator of the ULABG Biogeography Laboratory; founding editor-in-chief of the journal ''Herpetotropicos'';<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite book |last1=Sanchez-Villagra |first1=Marcelo R. |title=Venezuela Paleontologica |date=2012 |publisher=Universität Zürich |location=Switzerland |isbn=978-3-033-03606-2 |page=358 |edition=1 |url=https://www.msanchezlab.net/_files/venezuela_paleontologica/ven_pal_prol.pdf |access-date=30 December 2022}}</ref> head of the Department of Physical Geography and acting director of the School of Geography in the Faculty of Forest and Environmental Sciences at ULA. He currently directs the REVA Conservation Center (Rescue of Venezuelan Amphibian Species). He is a member of the Amphibian Specialist Group of the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).<ref name=lamarca>{{cite web |url=http://animalesamenazados.provita.org.ve/content/enrique-la-marca |title=Detalles del CV en Animales Amenazados de Provita |access-date=28 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180929000407/http://animalesamenazados.provita.org.ve/content/enrique-la-marca |archive-date=29 September 2018}}</ref>

==Honors==
He has received various recognitions in different programs for research and teaching promotion by Venezuelan institutions such as the Fondo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Tecnológicas (FONACIT) and the University of the Andes, Mérida: Programa de Promoción del Investigador (PPI), Programa de Estímulo al Investigador (PEI), Comisión Nacional para el Beneficio Académico (CONABA), and the Comisión Nacional de Desarrollo de la Educación Superior (CONADES).<ref>{{cite book |title=Reptiles de los Andes de Venezuela |date=2004 |publisher=Fundación Polar, Fundación BIOGEOS |location=Venezuela |isbn=980-379-083-8 |page=Back cover |edition=1 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/262876546_Reptiles_de_Los_Andes_de_Venezuela |access-date=30 December 2022}}</ref>
